# Devices

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_device_catalog.py from lu_alert/constants.py. Do not edit by hand: run the tool. -->

The plugin creates the devices below. No unit number ever changes once released, so an upgrade keeps every device, its history, scenes, scripts and schedules.

Every device is created when missing (at start and at every poll) and in use from the start; counters show their unit. All devices are read-only: the plugin shows what the feed says and sends nothing back.

## Summary (units 1-2)

The two devices to look at first: how many alerts there are and how bad the worst one is.

| Unit | Name | Type | Unit label | Shows |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Active Alerts | Custom Sensor | alerts | the number of alerts in force after all filters (minimum severity, location, ignored categories) |
| 2 | Highest Severity | Alert, read-only | - | the colour and the text of the most severe active alert (same text as *Alert 1*); green "No active alerts" when there is none |

## Switches for notifications and scripts (units 3-8)

On/Off switches that only *show* a state: use them as the condition of a notification, a scene or a dzVents script. They cannot be switched by hand; a command is answered with the real state.

| Unit | Name | Type | Unit label | Shows |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | Critical Alert Active | Switch (On/Off), read-only | - | On while at least one *Extreme* or *Severe* alert is active |
| 4 | Severe Alert Active | Switch (On/Off), read-only | - | On while at least one *Severe* alert is active |
| 5 | Extreme Alert Active | Switch (On/Off), read-only | - | On while at least one *Extreme* alert is active |
| 6 | Local Alert Active | Switch (On/Off), read-only | - | On while the area of an active alert contains your home (needs the location filter) |
| 7 | Watchlist Match | Switch (On/Off), read-only | - | On while the text of an active alert contains one of your watchlist keywords |
| 8 | Allergen Match | Switch (On/Off), read-only | - | On while the text of an active alert contains one of your allergens |

## Feed (units 9-10)

Whether the plugin can read the feed. A failing feed never clears the alerts: the alert devices keep the last known alerts (they still end when their end time passes) and *Feed Info* says since when the feed is not reachable.

| Unit | Name | Type | Unit label | Shows |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 9 | LU-Alert Status | Switch (On/Off), read-only | - | the connection: On while polls succeed, Off while they fail |
| 10 | Feed Info | Text, read-only | - | the state of the last poll: `OK 12:05: 12 files (1 new), 2 active`, or since when the feed is not reachable |

## Counters per severity (units 21-25)

One counter per severity, for graphs and for rules such as "two or more Moderate alerts".

| Unit | Name | Type | Unit label | Shows |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 21 | Extreme Alerts | Custom Sensor | alerts | the number of active *Extreme* alerts |
| 22 | Severe Alerts | Custom Sensor | alerts | the number of active *Severe* alerts |
| 23 | Moderate Alerts | Custom Sensor | alerts | the number of active *Moderate* alerts |
| 24 | Minor Alerts | Custom Sensor | alerts | the number of active *Minor* alerts |
| 25 | Information Alerts | Custom Sensor | alerts | the number of active *Information* alerts |

## Alert 1 ... Alert 10 (units 11-20)

One Alert device per active alert, the most severe first (of equal severity the newest first). Each shows a colour and a text such as `[Severe] Storm warning for the whole country - until 2026-11-02 14:00 | Strong winds are expected ...`: severity, headline, end time and, as far as the 200 characters of a Domoticz text allow, the start of the description (`LU_DEVICE_DESCRIPTION=0` in `.env` leaves it out). A slot without an alert is green and says *No alert*.

Only the first 3 are created (`LU_ALERT_DEVICES` in `.env`, 1-10); the *Active Alerts* counter and the per-severity counters always count all alerts. A slot above the configured number that exists from an earlier setting turns grey and says *Not in use (raise LU_ALERT_DEVICES in .env)*; it is never deleted by the plugin.

| Unit | Name | Type |
|---:|---|---|
| 11 | Alert 1 | Alert, read-only |
| 12 | Alert 2 | Alert, read-only |
| 13 | Alert 3 | Alert, read-only |
| 14 | Alert 4 | Alert, read-only |
| 15 | Alert 5 | Alert, read-only |
| 16 | Alert 6 | Alert, read-only |
| 17 | Alert 7 | Alert, read-only |
| 18 | Alert 8 | Alert, read-only |
| 19 | Alert 9 | Alert, read-only |
| 20 | Alert 10 | Alert, read-only |

## Colours

The colour of *Highest Severity* and of the *Alert n* devices follows the severity of the alert:

| Severity | Colour | Domoticz alert level |
|---|---|---:|
| Extreme | red | 4 |
| Severe | red | 4 |
| Moderate | orange | 3 |
| Minor | yellow | 2 |
| Information | green | 1 |
| Unknown | grey | 0 |
| Test | grey | 0 |

The severity comes from the LU-Alert *level* of the message when it has one, otherwise from the CAP `severity` field; see [LU-ALERT-DATA.md](LU-ALERT-DATA.md) for the level table and all rules.

## How the devices behave

- Values are written when they change, and every 300 seconds even when they did not, so Domoticz' sensor time-out never marks a quiet sensor as dead.
- A name or a visibility you set in Domoticz is never changed by the plugin; it only writes values.
- A device you delete in Domoticz is created again on the next poll.
- A text is cut to 200 characters, the most Domoticz can keep.
- Domoticz refuses new devices while *Setup > Settings > System > Accept new Hardware Devices* is off. The plugin says so once in the log and asks again every 5 minutes, so the devices appear as soon as the setting is on, without restarting the hardware.
